title: Valid Brackets

concept.title: A stack: last in, first out
body: A **stack** is a pile: you can only put an item on top (**push**) or take the top item away (**pop**); the item you added last is the first to leave (*last in, first out*). In Python a list works as a stack (`append` and `pop`), in C++ `vector` or `stack`, in Java `ArrayDeque`.

Brackets are the classic use. Every closing bracket must close the **most recent** bracket that is still open, which is exactly the top of a stack. Push each opening bracket. For a closing bracket check that the stack is not empty and that its top is the matching opening bracket, then pop it.
The final check `not stack` matters: a word such as `((` never fails inside the loop but leaves open brackets behind.

statement: A word consists of the brackets `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{` and `}`. It is **valid** if every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same kind, and brackets are closed in the correct order. Print `yes` if the word is valid, otherwise `no`.

examples.note: The bracket ] closes [ while ( is still open: not valid.

hints: Push every opening bracket on a stack.
A closing bracket must match the bracket on the top of the stack; then pop it.
At the end the stack must be empty.

explanation: Each closing bracket must match the most recent unclosed opening bracket, the top of the stack. The word is valid when no mismatch happens and the stack is empty at the end.
